prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE isolated transparent game sprite: the old skeletal remains of a fallen human adventurer lying face down on a dungeon floor, viewed from behind and slightly above, as a first-person dungeon crawler would see them while approaching. The skull and outstretched skeletal arms are furthest away at the TOP of the sprite; the spine, ribcage, pelvis, loosely bent legs and boots are closest to the viewer at the BOTTOM. Whole prone body fully visible, natural modest foreshortening; no upright character, no standing skeleton, no horizontal side-view. Match the attached medieval woodblock reference EXACTLY: irregular dark ink outlines, sparse carved hatching, worn printed marks, pale warm parchment bones, a few remnants of ragged dirty orange cloth. A battered bucket helm rests beside the skull. Simple readable small in-game memorial, not a monster and not grotesque. No flesh, gore, scary face or glowing eyes. The pose/composition is like the fallen knight at bottom left of image 2, but skeletal old remains with little remaining fabric. Leave clear transparent padding on all sides. Background TRULY transparent, no floor rectangle, no paper rectangle, no cast shadow. Bones are opaque pale parchment inside, holes between bones are transparent. No text, labels, border or UI. Image 1 style reference; image 2 only prone body orientation reference. Draw only ONE single fallen skeleton, not a sheet, no other assets.
